title: Prove meaning search on the owner's real mail

proofs.run: on the installed build with the real account, after the sync and the indexing have finished: read from a private copy of the owner's data folder, as numbers only: (a) stored messages, (b) messages in the word index, (c) chunks embedded in the meaning index, (d) chunks stored

in the installed build search the word 'cadeau' (absent from the mail, close in meaning to a word the mail holds); read the number of results and whether the first result is the message the owner knows to be about gifts
proofs.pass: results greater than 0 and the owner confirms the right message

owner: This is the owner's own mail on the owner's installed build: the lead can read counts (messages, word-index entries, meaning-index chunks) from a private copy, but only the owner can say that a search for 'cadeau' returns the right message. Run the installed build, let it finish indexing, search 'cadeau', and say what you see.
notes: What proves the engines in the repo (not the owner's data): word index inside words engine_search_inside.rs, meaning recall core/crates/search-vector/tests/recall_probe.rs, key by chunk id replies_d21.rs:88. The earlier reader could not read the data folder (the brief forbids it); I did not either. The exact index file names and tables of the data folder are not named here because I did not read them: the lead names them from docs/DATA-MAP.md rows 'chunk' (:145) and the search index rows when preparing the private copy. A meaning-index count equal to the number of stored chunks, and a word-index count equal to stored messages, are the acceptance's 'covering every stored message'.
